title: Working at Redwood: roles, career ladders, benefits, hiring & onboarding, internal tools
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

This page provides a single-source reference for working at Redwood: core values and expectations, role definitions and career ladders, benefits and perks, the hiring and onboarding process, and the internal tools you will use on day-to-day work. It is intended for all new hires, hiring managers, and people-ops partners.

1) Working at Redwood — culture and expectations

Summary:
- Mission-aligned: We prioritize shipping dependable, high-performance inference for customers. Engineers and product teams should favor reliability and reproducibility in designs.
- Collaboration-first: Cross-functional ownership (product, infra, research, SRE) is expected.
- Data-driven decisions: Use experiments, benchmarks, and postmortems to guide tradeoffs.

Core expectations:
- Shipping cadence: Deliver incremental improvements with clear rollouts, e.g., feature flags and canaries for model and infra changes.
- Documentation: Every service change must include a short design note and runbook updates.
- Blameless postmortems: Incidents are learning opportunities — focus on systemic fixes.

Onboarding checklist (high level):
1. Complete HR tasks (payroll, benefits enrollment, ID, NDA).
2. Security & compliance training (SSO, MFA, data handling).
3. Team-specific orientation: meet the manager, review team roadmap, pair on first ticket.
4. Tools access: git, internal confluence, Slack, CI/CD, cloud console.
5. First 30/60/90 plan: agree outcomes with manager.

2) Roles & career ladders

This section summarizes core role families at Redwood and the career ladder progression expectations. For complete job profiles see the role-specific pages under /confluence/org/roles.

Role families (summary):
- Engineering: infra, serving runtime, platform, private deployments, developer experience, SRE.
- Product: product management, design, data/product analytics.
- Research/Applied ML: model onboarding, quantization, evals.
- Go-to-market: growth, sales, solutions engineering.
- People Ops & Finance: recruiting, benefits, payroll, legal.

Career ladder templates (individual contributor track):
- IC1 (New grad / entry): Learns codebase, delivers small features with mentorship.
- IC2 (Mid): Owns components, writes reliable code, participates in design reviews.
- IC3 (Senior): Leads large features, mentors others, influences architecture and reliability tradeoffs.
- IC4 (Staff): Cross-team technical leadership, drives system-level initiatives, sets standards.
- IC5 (Principal): Company-level technical strategy, deep domain expertise, public-facing representation.

Manager track template:
- M1 (Engineering Manager): Leads a single team, people management, delivery accountability.
- M2 (Senior Manager): Manages managers or multiple teams, influences roadmap and resourcing.
- M3 (Director): Sets cross-functional strategy, owns organizational outcomes.

Promotion guidance (high level):
- Promotion evidence should span impact, leadership, execution quality, and scope.
- Typical artifact set: promotion packet, peer reviews, manager writeup, examples of shipped initiatives, mentoring evidence.
- Timeline: promotions are based on demonstrated readiness rather than strict time-in-role; discuss with your manager and people-ops.

3) Benefits & perks (2026-2027 summary)

Core benefits:
- Health: Medical, dental, and vision plans with multiple carrier options. Redwood covers a competitive share of premiums; dependents covered.
- Financial: 401(k) with company matching up to 4%; equity grants are issued at hire and recurring refresh grants for ongoing contributors.
- Paid time off: Flexible vacation policy, 12 company holidays + winter break, parental leave (16 weeks primary, 6 weeks secondary) plus phased return support.
- Family & wellness: Fertility benefits, mental health EAP, wellness stipend ($300/year).

Perks & allowances:
- Home office stipend: $1,200 one-time for home setup, $125/month remote work stipend.
- Learning & conferences: $2,000/year learning budget + time allocation for approved conferences.
- Commuter/parking and regional allowances where applicable for office-based teams.

Eligibility and enrollment:
- New hires must enroll in benefits within 30 days of start to avoid default coverage. For details, see the benefits portal page and payroll FAQ.

4) Hiring & onboarding overview

High-level hiring process (people-ops + hiring manager responsibilities):
1. Requisition & approval: Hiring manager opens req with role profile and compensation band; people-ops verifies budget and headcount.
2. Sourcing & screening: Recruiter sources candidates; initial phone screen for culture and baseline skills.
3. Interview loop: Technical interviews, take-home assignment (if applicable), cross-functional collaboration round, manager and peer interviews.
4. Decision & offer: Hiring committee reviews packet; offer extended by recruiter with compensation and equity details.
5. Background & compliance checks: Completed before start date.
6. Onboarding: Equipment ship, accounts provisioning, orientation sessions scheduled.

Interview best practices for interviewers:
- Use calibrated rubrics aligned to the role profile.
- Focus on evidence-based evaluation: ask for concrete examples and assess tradeoff reasoning.
- Respect candidate time; provide timely feedback and clear next steps.

New-hire 90-day onboarding plan (template):
- Day 0-7: Complete HR tasks, security training, meet immediate team members, set up dev environment, first small code review.
- Week 2-4: Ship first small ticket, attend product and roadmap syncs, set 30-day goals with manager.
- Month 2: Take ownership of a component, start participating in on-call rotations (if applicable), begin contributing to team architecture discussions.
- Month 3: Deliver a measurable project milestone, present learnings to the team, agree 6-month development plan.

Onboarding checklist (detailed table format as plain text):
- Accounts: Git (repo access), CI/CD (build/test runner), Slack, Confluence, Jira/Tickets, Cloud console, Secrets manager, Internal package registry.
- Hardware: Laptop provisioned, monitor and peripherals, VPN or hardware tokens if required.
- Training: Security, privacy, incident response, code-of-conduct, D&I intro.
- Mentorship: Assigned buddy and manager check-ins scheduled weekly for first month.

5) Internal tools guide — quick reference

This section lists common internal tools, purpose, and how to get started. All tool access requests should follow the access-and-permissions process in the security-and-compliance section.

- GitHub (repos.redwood): Primary code host. Request access via /jira/INFR-ACCESS or the repo's OWNERS file. Common commands: git clone git@github.com:redwood/<repo>.git, git checkout -b feature/ID. CI: PRs must pass unit tests and linters.

- CI/CD (Buildkite): Build pipelines and deployment orchestration. Key commands: bk pipeline triggers, view logs at ci.redwood/builds/<pipeline>. Use feature flags for safe rollout.

- Cloud Console (AWS/GCP): Provisioning and debugging resources. Use tagged roles and least-privilege IAM groups. Always follow deployment runbooks for stateful changes.

- Monitoring & Alerts (Datadog): Dashboards: service-latency, token-cost-per-model, error-rate. Pager rotation is handled by SRE; severity definitions are in the oncall-and-incident-response section.

- Secret Manager (Vault/KMS): Store keys and credentials. Never commit secrets to git. Use the secrets-access workflow for temporary access.

- Confluence & Knowledge base: Author pages in the company-handbook or team spaces. Use templates for runbooks and postmortems.

- Internal CLI (rwdctl): Centralized helper for common operations. Example:
  - rwdctl auth login
  - rwdctl infra provision --env staging --pool gpu-dedicated
  - rwdctl models deploy --model-id redwood/opt-xx --variant quantized

6) Compensation & performance cycles

Performance review cadence:
- Bi-annual reviews with a calibrated calibration cycle. Managers submit review packets including goals, 360 feedback, and impact artifacts.

Compensation adjustments:
- Base salary adjustments occur at promotion or through annual salary review cycles. Equity refresh grants are given annually to employees meeting performance and retention criteria.

7) Frequently asked questions (FAQ)

Q: Who do I contact for payroll issues?
A: Payroll & benefits inquiries -> benefits@redwood.com (people-ops).

Q: How do I request ergonomic equipment?
A: Submit a ticket to IT with manager approval and attach receipts for reimbursement if post-purchase.

Q: What is our parental leave policy?
A: Primary caregivers receive 16 weeks paid leave; secondary caregivers 6 weeks. Contact people-ops for individual accommodation.

8) Ownership and escalation

Document owner: People Ops (owner: Ava Martinez). Please direct content updates, corrections, or accessibility requests to people-ops@redwood.com.

Escalation contacts:
- Urgent payroll or benefits errors: benefits@redwood.com
- Security or data incidents: security-incident@redwood.com (follow incident process).
- Onboarding blockers (access or hardware): it-support@redwood.com, cc people-ops.
